title: What should AsmAI do when sign-in or subscription access is unavailable?
body: The installer signs into each provider on the machine running the agents, including a remote host. Credentials can expire or usage limits can be reached during a job.
recommendation: AsmAI checks readiness without exposing credentials. If access is missing, expired, or exhausted, pause affected work and give instructions to sign in or restore access; keep independent authorized work running. Never switch billing sources or providers automatically. Do not copy login tokens between machines; the installer establishes access on each execution host.
options: Use this installer-owned sign-in and pause policy
Automatically switch to another configured subscription provider
Use a different policy — describe below

title: How configurable should provider staffing be in v1?
body: Both providers will be supported. We still need to decide whether a factory must use one provider everywhere or may assign providers differently across roles and workers.
recommendation: Allow a configured provider/model for each role leader and a worker default for each role, with explicit assignment overrides. A started assignment keeps its chosen provider/model; changing configuration affects new assignments. Do not promise provider-native conversation portability between Claude and Codex.
options: Mixed leaders and workers with explicit assignment overrides
One provider per role, shared by its leader and workers
One provider for the whole factory at a time

title: How should supported runtime versions be defined?
body: The local versions observed are Codex 0.157.0 and Claude Code 2.1.283. Seeing a version installed does not prove the adapter works with it. Provider updates can change events, approvals, or resume behavior.
recommendation: Publish explicit tested runtime/adapter combinations and record actual versions. Treat the observed versions as candidates only. Refuse unsupported combinations with an actionable message rather than promising all future versions work. Qualify upgrades deliberately; do not silently update provider runtimes.
options: Allow untested versions with a warning
Always follow the latest installed provider version
